question: Which standardized unit does a centiliter map to: 10 milliliters (standard_unit milliliter, standard_quantity 10) or 0.01 liters (standard_unit liter, standard_quantity 0.01)?
readings: standard_unit "milliliter" with standard_quantity 10, like the other small volume units.
standard_unit "liter" with standard_quantity 0.01, since a centiliter is defined as a hundredth of a liter.
rationale: Both existing volume standards (milliliter with quantity 1 and liter with quantity 1) are available as a base and the request gives the centiliter's value in both, so an engineer must pick one; the choice changes the stored standard_unit of every centiliter unit and how conversions are computed. The target test asserts standard_unit == "milliliter" and standard_quantity == 10.
